title: ES Modules
summary: ES modules split code across files. Each file is its own module with its own scope. Values must be explicitly exported to be used in other files, and explicitly imported. There are two export styles: named exports (a file can have many) and a default export (a file can have at most one). React projects use one component per file with a default export for the component and named exports for helpers or constants.
keyPoints: Named export: export const x = ...  or  export function fn() {}
Named import: import { x, fn } from './file'
Default export: export default MyComponent  (one per file)
Default import: import MyComponent from './MyComponent'  (name is up to the importer)
Both in one line: import React, { useState } from 'react'
Rename a named import: import { formatTitle as format } from './utils'
Avoid import * as — it prevents tree shaking
Convention: one React component per file, default exported; helpers named-exported

exercises.prompt:
A file movies.js contains:

export const API_KEY = 'abc'
export function formatTitle(t, y) { return `${t} (${y})` }

How do you import both in another file?
exercises.explanation: Both are named exports, so they are imported with curly braces {}. Without braces you would be importing the default export (which does not exist in this file).
Default exports are imported without curly braces. The name you use locally is your choice — it doesn't have to match the exported function name.

exercises.prompt: How many default exports can one file have?
exercises.explanation: A file can have at most one default export. It can have any number of named exports.
Both are named exports, so they are imported with curly braces {}. Multiple named imports are comma-separated. Without braces you would be trying to import a default export, which doesn't exist here.

exercises.prompt:
A file utils.js has:

export function formatTitle(t, y) {}
export default []

In main.js, you want to import both the default export as movies AND formatTitle. Which is correct?
options: import movies from './utils'; import { formatTitle } from './utils'
Both A and C are correct
exercises.answer: Both A and C are correct
exercises.explanation: You can combine a default import and named imports in one statement (A), or use two separate import statements (C). Both produce the same result.
